articles.title: Tom Brady's NFL Power Rankings: The GOAT Is Taking A Mini Victory Lap With New No. 1
articles.summary: Tom Brady has a new No. 1 in his power rankings, and he's taking extra pride in being right about this team (so far).
articles.body: Tom Brady knows that Super Bowls aren't won in October, but you can get an "I told you so" or two during the fall. That's what the seven-time Super Bowl champion did when he unveiled his most recent power rankings. With the San Francisco 49ers losing to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, Brady has a new team at No. 1 ahead of Week 8, saying that he's taking a "mini victory lap" as a result. Brady's new No. 1 team doesn't reside in the AFC North, even though the division has four teams with a winning record. In fact, Brady doesn't have any of the four teams from that division in his top 10, suggesting they're the first four teams out in his power rankings this week. But Brady is enjoying how competitive the AFC North is. "Let's put the AFC North in an 18-week round-robin every single year, and the winner of it slots into the division round," Brady said. "You guys cool with that?" Here's a full look at Brady's top 10 this week. 10. Jacksonville JaguarsRecord: 4-2Previous ranking: 8 ↓ Week 7 result: Idle Brady's thoughts: Jacksonville got a bye to travel back from London. You gotta go 1-0 against jet lag in that situation. They're back Sunday against the Colts with a 2.5-game lead in the AFC South and, by midseason standards, a relatively healthy roster. If Trevor Lawrence keeps up this level of play, this division could turn into a runaway in a hurry. Liam Coen's the right guy to keep those guys in that aggressive mentality. I'm very impressed with what Liam's done as head coach. Hats off to Liam. He was a great coordinator for one year, moved on to head coach and he hasn't missed a beat. Up next: vs. Indianapolis Colts (Sunday) 9. New England PatriotsRecord: 4-3Previous ranking: 4 ↓ Week 7 result: 30-24 loss at Chicago Bears Brady's thoughts: Drake Maye dueled with Caleb Williams. It was a great game Thursday night in Chicago, and we don't get enough of those throughout the year. So that was a nice treat. They couldn't get the road win in the end, but I still consider this a very strong showing for New England in one of the toughest — yeah, you got it, Chicago — one of the toughest primetime environments in the league. Drake's last four games: 12 tuddies, two picks. They got a good chance to get back in the win column in Miami on Sunday. Up next: at Miami Dolphins (Sunday) 8. Detroit LionsRecord: 4-2Previous ranking: Unranked ↑ Week 7 result: 20-17 win vs. Green Bay Packers Brady's thoughts: You guys remember a few weeks ago when I called the Lions the most fun team in football to watch? Well, we got to show the whole country as Jared Goff and co. won a thriller against Green Bay in Detroit. The Jared-to-Jameson Williams connection is on fire right now — four touchdowns in their last two games. KB (Kevin Burkhardt) and I will be back in the booth on Sunday for an NFC North collision with the Vikings. One of the best offenses in the NFL going against the best defense in the NFL. Heart medication will be on deck, KB. I can't wait for this one. It's (the Vikings' defense) as tough as it gets, and it all starts with a lot of film study this week, a lot of walkthroughs, a lot of preparation for that Lions offense. Jared Goff's doing such a great job as a field general, sorting protections out, making sure he's got all the blocking assignments pre-snap, but then it comes down to post-snap. How does the line from the Lions handle these different looks, and ultimately, these very good rushers on this Minnesota defense? It's going to be a tough battle all day. Up next: vs. Minnesota Vikings (Sunday) 7. Seattle SeahawksRecord: 4-3Previous ranking: 9 ↑ Week 7 result: 20-3 win vs. Kansas City Chiefs Brady's thoughts: Seattle handed the Chiefs their first loss of the year with a dominant defensive performance, completely shutting down K9 (Kenneth Walker III) and that rushing offense. JSN (Jaxon Smith-Njigba) did what he always does, going for 150 yards and a tuddy, which should give Sam Darnold some much-needed confidence going forward. The Seahawks got another tough one against the Bears in a massive Monday night game, but we'll see if the defending champs can really get on a roll. Up next: vs. Chicago Bears (Monday) 6. Denver BroncosRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 6 Week 7 result: 30-16 win at Arizona Cardinals Brady's thoughts: Another week, another Broncos win — and it's not always pretty. It's actually almost never pretty, but who cares when you're winning games? Their only two losses came against the Niners and the Chiefs, so it's hard to find a hole in that résumé. And now Kansas City, the team that beat them 31-10 in Week 1, heads to Denver on Sunday. That's a chance to make a real statement in the AFC. Up next: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday) 5. Chicago BearsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 7 ↑ Week 7 result: 30-24 win vs. New England Patriots Brady's thoughts: We talked about Thursday night already, and Caleb Williams has been hot since coming back from that hamstring. He got 300 yards, no turnovers on Thursday and I really don't think any team is having more fun celebrating their postgame wins than the Bears. And how long until Ben Johnson is popping the top again? As we go down the list, I'm realizing we've got an insane slate of games this weekend, so don't be surprised if we shake things up in next week's rankings. Can Chicago go from No. 5 to No. 1 with a win in Seattle? I'm just saying. Up next: at Seattle Seahawks (Monday) 4. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 5-1Previous ranking: 2 ↓ Week 7 result: 20-3 loss at Seattle Seahawks Brady's thoughts: Be honest, you were thinking it — we were all thinking it: Was Kansas City about to rip off, like, 12 straight to start the season? Lucky for the AFC West, the answer is no, as the Chiefs stall out in Seattle. Pat Mahomes had a rough night, and it doesn't happen often. But after the way this offense has played all year, we can cut them all some slack. I have no doubt Pat is itching to get back out on the field in Denver and make things right. That's the kind of leader he is. Kickstart that offense early, give Pat some time to work receivers open, and yeah, I'll say it: Can we make some field goals, guys? Up next: at Denver Broncos (Sunday) 3. Buffalo BillsRecord: 5-1Previous ranking: 5 ↑ Week 7 result: Idle Brady's thoughts: The Bills come off a bye with an extra week to get ready for the Ravens, and they might be getting Lamar Jackson back. Thank God. For the sake of the fans, please give us Josh Allen vs. Lamar. A full-strength Baltimore offense would be a great test for a defense that's really struggled this year. Luckily, the offense leads the league in points per game, so it can usually make up for it. They moved into a tie atop the AFC with that Chiefs loss, and now they can create some daylight and prove the conference goes through Buffalo. Up next: vs. Baltimore Ravens (Sunday) 2. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 1 ↓ Week 7 result: 29-20 loss at Atlanta Falcons Brady's thoughts: Down go the Niners, not very far, and I may have jinxed this last one last week when I said they'll cruise into their bye at a perfect 7-0. It was one of my first announcer jinxes. My bad, guys. They get a well-timed bye this week because the injuries continue to pile up for the Niners. But as I've said before, I think Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch have built a team capable of withstanding it. Brock Purdy was not great in Atlanta, simple as that, and I know he'll be in the film room and ready to go next time out. It's all about pliability. Get in there, get those muscles worked out, relieve the tension and be ready to go in a few weeks. Up next: Bye 1. Minnesota VikingsRecord: 6-0Previous ranking: 3 ↑ Week 7 result: 16-10 win vs. Indianapolis Colts Brady's thoughts: Someone alert the media: We've got a new No. 1 in the Tom Brady Power Rankings as the Minnesota Vikings beat the Colts to stay unbeaten. I'm taking a mini victory lap here. We were getting some heat early when I had the Vikings up with the Niners and Chiefs of the world, but they're backing it up. Like I've talked about with Denver, the offense is far from efficient at this point, and they'll have to figure that out fast. But they're well coached, they get after the quarterback, they take the ball away and they're rallying around Kyler Murray. We're going to learn a lot about this team in Detroit on Sunday, and I will be there at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Up next: at Detroit Lions (Sunday) FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Raiders' Ashton Jeanty Shades Unnamed Jets' Defenders in Video, 'Don't Really Want to Tackle'
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty thinks his team will benefit in Week 8 by what he described as a lack of effort from the New York Jets run defense.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty thinks his team will benefit in Week 8 by what he described as a lack of effort from the New York Jets run defense.

"I think we can definitely get the run game going, get back on track, just really get after this guys," Jeanty told reporters ahead of the Sunday matchup.

"Couple of guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."

Javonte Carries Cowboys Back Into Race 😤

Jets defensive back Jarvis Brownlee clapped back at Jeanty on Thursday:

The Raiders are preparing to kick off the Week 8 matchup Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in New Jersey.

Jeanty has seen his production drop in his sophomore NFL season while serving as the lead rusher in one of the leagues' least effective rushing attacks.

He has recorded 328 rushing yards and a touchdown on 106 carries so far this season while seeing his yards per attempt (3.1) and yards per game (46.9) decline from his 2025 rookie campaign.

The former first-round pick was most recently held to a season-low eight carries and 15 yards in the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the visiting Los Angeles Rams.

With Mike Washington Jr. as the only other back seeing significant carries and quarterback Kirk Cousins focusing on the pass game, the Raiders have ranked 31st in the NFL in total yards on the ground during the team's 3-4 start to the season.

The Jets defense has allowed the ninth-most rushing yards against in the NFL during their own 2-5 run.

New York most recently allowed the Miami Dolphins to gain 156 yards on the ground in the team's first win of the season last weekend. The Dolphins' Ollie Gordon II forced a career-high 10 missed tackles (h/t NFL Next Gen Stats cited by FinsXtra ) in the win.

The Jets lost one of their top interior run defenders in that game when T'Vondre Sweat suffered a knee injury.

Sweat's potential absence could potentially create a larger role for rookie defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr., who boasts one of the highest run stop rates among NFL interior defensive linemen so far this season (h/t FanSided's Justin Fried ).

Another step forward from Jackson and more consistency from veterans like Demario Davis, who said after the loss to the Dolphins he felt the Jets had shown "character" and "resilience" this season, could help the Jets team bounce back from the loss to the Dolphins by shutting down Jeanty this weekend.

articles.title: Week 8 Fantasy Football Cheat Sheet for Deep Sleepers to Grab on Waiver Wire
articles.summary: We're rapidly approaching the midway point of the 2026 NFL season, which means that fantasy football playoffs are right around the corner. To this point, managers have been forced to navigate a cascade of injuries, along with the usual bye-week blues. The trend will continue in Week 8.
articles.body:
We're rapidly approaching the midway point of the 2026 NFL season, which means that fantasy football playoffs are right around the corner. To this point, managers have been forced to navigate a cascade of injuries, along with the usual bye-week blues. The trend will continue in Week 8.

The Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers will be on bye this week.

The good news is that a few viable sleepers should still be available on the waiver wire entering Thursday's matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers.

Here, you'll find updated rankings for Week 8, a cheat sheet for value plays, and a look at some top sleeper options who may still be available to pick up.

All rankings and picks are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

Wire Target: Geno Smith, QB, New York Jets

Managers looking for a spot starter at quarterback should consider Geno Smith in Week 8. While the New York Jets' starter hasn't been a top performer every week, he's started to develop a strong bond with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. and should have a solid floor moving forward.

In last week's loss to the Miami Dolphins, Smith threw three touchdown passes and delivered 24.5 fantasy points. He could replicate that success this week against a fading Las Vegas Raiders defense.

The Raiders have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season, and they could be even more sluggish than usual this week. Cross-country trips and early afternoon games rarely benefit West Coast teams.

Smith is still only rostered in 21 percent of fantasy leagues.

Wire Target: Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

The Washington Commanders have lost Terry McLaurin to a season-ending knee injury. This will likely move Stefon Diggs into the No. 1 receiver role and rookie wideout Antonio Williams into the No. 2 spot.

There's a very real chance that Williams is the biggest beneficiary when it comes to fantasy football.

Yet, Williams is still only rostered in 12 percent of leagues. That's likely to change after Week 8, though.

The rookie had a solid eight-point outing in his last game and could easily reach double digits this week against the rival Philadelphia Eagles. Philly has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Bears' Caleb Williams Says He'll Continue to Wear Unapproved Caddix Cleats Despite NFL Fine
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has no plans of switching out his Caddix cleats despite the NFL fining him for wearing an unauthorized brand in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has no plans of switching out his Caddix cleats despite the NFL fining him for wearing an unauthorized brand in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.

Williams, who does not have an endorsement deal with Caddix, told reporters he intends to keep wearing the cleats during games in part because they have helped protect his legs and feet from injuries:

"I'm huge into trying to stay on the field. I'm huge into trying to be healthy. It's a rough game and things like that. So the cleats, they've been great. They've been super comfy and they've worked. They are a science type of cleat. It's something that focuses on when you plant on the hard plants on turf or grass, they call them SmartStuds, and they move when you move in these hard plants. They take tension off of your tendons, your joints and all of that. So over the course of a long career or over the course of a long year, when you can take some percentage -- it could be one, it could 50, it could be 12, it could be whatever, you know. When you take that percentage off consistently over a period of time, you know, you get to have the chance, a higher chance of being healthy. And so that's what I focus on. I try to be healthy. They're smart cleats. They're science cleats, and they've been working for me. A bunch of other guys wear them in the league, and they're forward-focused on making sure players stay on the field, and that's what I'm always focused on."

After the NFL announced on Monday that Williams was being fined $11,941 for wearing the cleats without covering up the logo, Caddix founder Jack Rasmussen said the brand would cover the amount and explained how the custom shoes help prevent against injuries.

"He bought our cleats because they're the only ones built with SmartStuds to release under injurious load, reducing the force responsible for non-contact knee and ankle injuries," Rasmussen said.

Per ESPN's Courtney Cronin , Williams has appealed the fine and Caddix will also have a hearing with the NFL on Nov. 10 about the decision.

Since the NFL currently has licensing deals with Nike, Under Armour and Adidas for footwear and gloves, those are the only brands players are allowed to wear with the logo showing during games.

Players can use branded items outside of those three, but the league requires the logo to be covered otherwise they are fined for violating the uniform and equipment policy.

Cronin noted Williams wore Nike brand cleats during his first two NFL seasons, but the Bears quarterback said he has been trying to switch to Caddix "for about a year."

Per the Caddix website , the brand was founded by the father-son duo of Jeff and Jack Rasmussen after researching non-contact ACL tears.

"They dug into decades of research and found a consistent culprit: the interaction between the cleat and the playing surface," according to the Caddix bio. "When a cleat locks the foot into the ground, rotational force is driven up the leg and into the knee, causing excessive strain and injury."

The brand cites 2025 as its "breakout" year when more than 30 NFL players began wearing the cleats during games.

Caddix lists Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp, Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid and Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jalen Ramsey among the athletes who use its cleats.

Williams has worn the cleats throughout the 2026 season. He missed three games from Weeks 3-5 due to a hamstring injury before returning on Oct. 18 against the Falcons.

The 24-year-old also wore Caddix cleats in Chicago's Week 7 win over the New England Patriots.

articles.title: Bears acquire DT Jeffery Simmons from Titans for a package which includes 2 first-round picks
articles.summary: Simmons is a three-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have acquired three-time All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, in a trade that was announced Thursday .

As part of the deal, the Bears are also receiving a 2028 fifth-round draft pick and are sending Tennessee first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick.

"There are few people like Jeff Simmons. We are forever grateful for all he has given this team and this city," Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk said in a statement. "His formidable presence on the field was surpassed only by what he did off it. He gave Nashville more than football. The Give 'Em A Reason Foundation has changed lives in Middle Tennessee and in Mississippi, and I have no doubt it will continue to wherever he goes. Jeff — thank you. For how you played, how you led, and how you represented our team."

Simmons, 29, is joining a Bears defense that has allowed the eighth-fewest total yards (313.4 per game), third-fewest rushing yards (87.6) and ninth-fewest points (20.4), plus has recorded the fifth-most sacks (18) through seven weeks.

Through seven games this season, Simmons has four sacks, 38 total tackles and one forced fumble.

As his name continually popped up in the rumor mill ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, he said this week he has not heard anything from the organization and that he expected to remain in Tennessee. One phone call has changed everything.

Simmons was a first-round selection out of Mississippi State by the Titans in 2019. Since he entered the NFL, he's been a nightmare for defenses and quarterbacks. In 106 career games, the four-time Pro Bowler has 46.5 sacks, 414 total tackles and 72 tackles for loss.

In June, Simmons signed a three-year, $105.8 million contract extension with the Titans with $100 million guaranteed.

The 5-2 Bears have won four of their last five games and sit in second place in the NFC North behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Jeffery Simmons Traded to Bears from Titans, Full Details Revealed for Blockbuster NFL Deal
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears made a massive splash on the trade market Thursday, reportedly acquiring defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears made a massive splash on the trade market Thursday, reportedly acquiring defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero first reported the deal.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Titans will acquire a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

Simmons to Chicago is the latest blockbuster NFL trade to go down this week after the Indianapolis Colts dealt guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday.

An anonymous NFC general manager texted NFL insider Jordan Schultz regarding the Simmons trade, saying, "Respect to the Bears for doing that. That offense with this defense now makes them a Super Bowl roster for this year and for years to come without a doubt."

The 29-year-old Simmons has been among the best defensive tackles in football for the past several seasons, securing four Pro Bowl nods in five seasons from 2021 to 2025.

Simmons is also a two-time Second Team All-Pro, and he was named a First Team All-Pro for the first time last season when he recorded a career-high 11 sacks to go along with 67 tackles, 17 tackles for loss and three forced fumbles.

Originally selected 19th overall by the Titans in the 2019 NFL draft out of Mississippi State, Simmons has registered 414 tackles, 46.5 sacks, 72 tackles for loss and nine forced fumbles in 106 career regular-season games.

That includes 38 tackles, four sacks, six tackles for loss and one forced fumble through seven games this season.

The Bears are vying for their second consecutive NFC North title, and they currently trail the undefeated Minnesota Vikings by 1.5 games for the division lead with a 5-2 record.

Under offensive guru and head coach Ben Johnson, the Bears rank third in the NFL in total offense and eighth in scoring offense, although they would likely be even higher had quarterback Caleb Williams not missed three games due to injury.

While offense is their strength, the Bears are also eighth in total defense and ninth in scoring defense, and they rank third in the NFL against the run.

Chicago has not gotten big-time production out of its defensive tackles, though, as Kentavius Street has just one sack and Grady Jarrett has none.

Simmons should provide a massive boost to the Bears' defensive interior, and although the price to acquire him was steep, he is the type of game-wrecker and difference-maker the unit needed.

Making the move even more exciting for Bears fans is the fact that Simmons is not a rental, as he is signed through the 2030 season.

articles.title: Bears, Titans' Updated Salary Caps, NFL Draft Picks, Depth Charts After Jeffery Simmons Trade
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans took another step toward a rebuild while the Chicago Bears set themselves up as a win-now team with the Thursday trade of All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans took another step toward a rebuild while the Chicago Bears set themselves up as a win-now team with the Thursday trade of All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

The Bears sent a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-rounder and a 2027 fourth-rounder to the Titans in order to acquire Simmons alongside a 2028 fifth-rounder, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Thursday.

The Titans are now set to hold nine picks in the upcoming draft, including two in the first round and five in the top four rounds, according to Tankathon .

Tennessee will join the New York Jets and Cleveland Browns as teams with multiple first-rounders in the upcoming draft.

The Titans are also on track to hold multiple first-round picks in the 2028 draft.

The Bears will be able to upgrade their defensive line with the addition of Simmons to the interior. Here's a look at Chicago's front four barring the return of Dayo Odeyingbo:

Simmons signed an extension in June that made him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history .

The Bears will be on the hook to pay Simmons $7.9 million this season before his deal balloons to $26.9 million in guaranteed money in 2027, per Spotrac.

That deal is currently guaranteed through 2027. Simmons will lock in his 2028 salary if he is still on the roster March 15.

The Titans took on dead cap hits of $14.1 million in 2026 and $20.8 million in 2027 by moving Simmons, per Spotrac's Mike Ginnitti .

Tennessee ultimately paid $25.3 million to have Simmons play seven games with the franchise this season, per Ginnitti.

The Bears are currently projected by Spotrac to have $2.7 million in 2026 cap space following the trade. The franchise may need to restructure ahead of the 2027 campaign, at which point Spotrac currently projects the team will be $41.7 million over the cap.

Spotrac projects the Titans will have $37.4 million in 2026 cap space and $83.3 million in 2027 cap space.

Simmons could instantly slot in as one of the most disruptive players in the Bears' defensive line.

The 33-year-old has recorded four sacks, six tackles for loss and nine quarterback hits in seven games with Tennessee, all of which would at least tie for the team lead in Chicago.

That continues a dominant run that has seen Simmons rank second only to Kansas City Chiefs star Chris Jones in sacks over the last six seasons.

The Bears have ranked eighth in the NFL with a 37.9 percent blitz rate so far this season, per Sharp Football . That could potentially change now that the Bears have added a player who ranks first among defensive tackles in ESPN's pass rush win rate .

Odeyingbo was placed on IR with a quadriceps injury earlier this month. The Bears will at least be bolstered in the short term by the return of Sweat, who has finished serving out a two-game suspension.

At least part of the Bears' new defensive line could make its debut Monday night in a Week 8 matchup at the Seattle Seahawks.

The Titans could be making more moves to stack up on draft capital ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler named edge rusher Jeremaine Johnson II, running back Tony Pollard and cornerback Alontae Taylor as players among the potential trade candidates going forward.

articles.title: Jeffery Simmons Trade Stuns NFL Fans as Bears Emerge as Major Super Bowl Contender in NFC
articles.summary: With Caleb Williams leveling up once again this season, the Chicago Bears clearly feel a Super Bowl window is open after making the biggest blockbuster of the trade-deadline season so far to acquire Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
With Caleb Williams leveling up once again this season, the Chicago Bears clearly feel a Super Bowl window is open after making the biggest blockbuster of the trade-deadline season so far to acquire Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Bears will send first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 plus a fourth-rounder in 2027 to the Titans in exchange for Simmons and 2028 fifth-round pick.

Off to a 5-2 start, including 3-1 in games started by Williams, the Bears adding arguably the best interior defensive lineman in the NFL has fans and analysts putting them in the top tier of Super Bowl contenders in the NFC.

In addition to fans and analysts hyping the Bears, people in the NFL are also very positive on the deal.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz quoted an NFC general manager who texted that Chicago's combination of offense with a Simmons-leg defense "makes them a Super Bowl roster for this year and for years to come without a doubt."

Through the first seven weeks of the 2026 season, the Bears are one of four teams that ranks in the top 10 in both points scored and points allowed per game. The other three are the San Francisco 49ers, Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Bears have primarily succeeded on defense thanks to a high blitz rate and reliance on turnovers. Their 37.9 percent blitz rate is the eighth-highest in the NFL and they are tied for seventh with 10 takeaways.

Two areas the Bears have struggled is down-to-down consistency and stopping the run. They rank 14th in defensive EPA per play and 19th in EPA per rush, per SumerSports.com .

Simmons is a pass-rushing savant from the interior, which will allow defensive coordinator Dennis Allen to ease up on some of his blitzing tendencies to create pressure from his front four.

The 29-year-old also leads all defensive tackles with 20 run stops in seven starts for the Titans this season.

After fellow NFC contenders in Seattle and San Francisco made moves earlier in the week for Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, respectively, the Bears responded by making the biggest blockbuster of the season thus far.

It's also plausible that we could see two of those traded players matchup in Week 8 with the Bears playing the Seahawks on Monday Night Football.

Simmons won't have a lot of time to get acclimated to his new defensive system ahead of time, but it wouldn't be a surprise to see him get some run as the Bears look to solidify their status as a Super Bowl contender by beating the reigning champs in Seattle.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Panthers and Packers try to rebound from frustrating losses
articles.summary: The Panthers and Packers are both at or hovering around.500 coming into Thursday night.
articles.body:
Is it worse to lose a close, heartbreaking game at the end or blown out? We could poll the Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers.

The two teams facing off Thursday night are coming off losses, and those defeats were much different. The Packers lost 20-17 to the Lions in Week 7, with many miscues, including a partially blocked field goal late in the game that would have tied it. Fans and players alike also had a lot of issues with the officiating .

While the Packers could look back at a play or two that might have turned the game, the Panthers were done by halftime. They trailed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 33-6 at halftime and lost 43-13 in a stunning blowout. The Panthers had looked like an improved team before whatever happened against the Buccaneers last weekend.

The Packers have had a strange season. They were not good for four weeks but escaped it with a 2-2 record. Then they blasted the Cowboys and Bears in back-to-back weeks before falling short against the Lions, though that's not a bad loss. The Panthers were 3-2 before the Buccaneers game with Bryce Young having a true breakout season. Young didn't play well against Tampa Bay but nobody on Carolina's side did. The Panthers have to show that performance was an anomaly, though they also had a loss to the Bears in which they gave up 59 points.

It's never a fun week for an NFL team after a loss. The best thing is to come back and play again right away. Both teams Thursday are more appreciative than normal for the short week.

The difference between the situation for these two teams could be as easy as this: The Panthers play in the mediocre NFC South, and the Packers play in the NFC North which might be the NFL's toughest division.

The Panthers don't want to fall behind .500, but there's not another team that will run away with that division. The Packers are already three losses behind the Vikings in the division, and the Bears and Lions are very tough, too.

Green Bay can't fall further behind in the North, especially with a home loss against an opponent it is favored to beat.

The Packers will have a lot more balance with Jacobs off the commissioner's exempt list. Jacobs wasn't efficient in his return against Detroit in Week 7 with just 36 rushing yards on 11 attempts, but he added 55 yards and a touchdown on five catches. The Packers' running game was going nowhere without him in the lineup.

While offensive line issues will continue to keep Green Bay from having a great rushing attack, at least it should keep defenses honest. There should be concern over how Jacobs plays on a short week, after not playing for the first six weeks. But he's facing a Panthers defense that gave up 258 rushing yards last weekend against the Buccaneers. Carolina gave up 291 rushing yards in Week 1 to Chicago and while the run defense had improved after that, Sunday's performance against Tampa Bay was troubling. Jacobs and the Packers will be testing that run defense early on.

This game was Packers -7 in the offseason, but has re-opened a combination of Green Bay -3.5 and -4 at sportsbooks — partially due to the fact that Carolina played one of the worst games of the season in a 43-13 loss as a 3-point home favorite against the Bucs. Keep an eye on WR Matthew Golden and DT Devonte Wyatt for the Packers, both of whom are questionable to play. The Panthers are a remarkable 13-0 ATS in their past 13 games after a loss.

It's hard for Carolina to play any worse than last week, so was that a bad game or a bad sign? I think it was more likely a momentary breakdown and that Bryce Young & Co. can hang with a banged-up Green Bay team and keep this within the number. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy managers are optimistic for Week 8's opener between the Panthers and Packers, as the total is set for 47.5. Here are three themes to consider as you enjoy the game.

1. Can Bryce Young get his groove back? Every time it feels like Young has fully entered the Circle of Trust, he seems to have a setback — Tampa Bay ate his lunch in Week 7. Green Bay's defense has been better than expected this year, especially against the pass.

2. What does Josh Jacobs do for an encore? Jacobs checked in with a solid RB11 finish in his season debut, though it was the receiving game where he made his mark. Running lanes might be harder to find behind a Green Bay offensive line that's played poorly.

3. How will the Carolina WR room play out? Although Jalen Coker was undrafted while Tetairoa McMillan was a first-round pick, the two players have produced at similar levels when both are on the field. Of course for either to hit his projection here, Young has to play better and Carolina's offensive line has to rebound from a messy game. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Bears' Updated Super Bowl LXI Odds After Jeffery Simmons Trade with Titans
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are going for it.
articles.body:
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Thursday the reigning NFC North champions are acquiring four-time Pro Bowler Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans at the cost of two first-round picks.

In the immediate aftermath of the deal, the Bears have the joint third-best Super Bowl odds (+1000) with the Seattle Seahawks at FanDuel Sportsbook .

With quarterback Caleb Williams still on his rookie contract, this is precisely the time for general manager Ryan Poles to be bold. Williams counts for $10.8 million against the salary cap right now and then $12.6 million for the 2027 season. Even his fifth-year option in 2028 will be less than the market value for an upper-tier QB.

Chicago is never going to have more flexibility to build around Williams than it does now.

Simmons addresses a big need along the defensive front.

Chicago is allowing the eighth-fewest yards per game (313.4) and boasts a top-five unit against the run. The defense is a more modest 22nd in yards per carry surrendered (4.4).

Poles is having to pay a high premium after the trade of Gervon Dexter Sr. left a void in the interior of the Bears' line.

It's not often that a defensive tackle is the proverbial missing piece of the puzzle, but that's how good Simmons can be as a member of the Monsters of the Midway. Through seven games this season, he has 38 combined tackles and four sacks. That latter number would tie for the most on the Bears.

For most fans, Chicago isn't the top Super Bowl favorite with Simmons now in the fold. The team does look like an even stronger contender, though.

articles.title: Week 8 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice on Fantasy Football Stars to Play or Bench
articles.summary: It's been an unusual season for fantasy footballers thus far, with injuries, surprising slumps, and unexpected breakouts shaking up the landscape weekly. We're likely to see more of the same in Week 8, which will open with Thursday night's game between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
It's been an unusual season for fantasy footballers thus far, with injuries, surprising slumps, and unexpected breakouts shaking up the landscape weekly. We're likely to see more of the same in Week 8, which will open with Thursday night's game between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers.

Managers can, of course, rely on their top draft picks, if healthy. However, plenty of stars are on the injury report, and several more will be on bye this week.

The Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers have Week 8 off.

Those looking to lean on second-tier stars can find some start/sit advice here, with picks based on recent production, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Even with a fair bit of scrambling upside, Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray has been a low-level streamer this season. He has topped 18 fantasy points only once and is coming off of an underwhelming 13.9-point performance against the Indianapolis Colts.

However, Murray has legitimate top-10 potential this week because of Minnesota's matchup and situation. The Vikings may have to go pass-heavy, as Aaron Jones continues to deal with an MCL sprain. They'll also face the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks than any other team.

Sit: Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers routed the Panthers in Week 7 while welcoming back Baker Mayfield from his dislocated thumb. However, Mayfield was far from 100 percent and attempted just 11 passes.

Mayfield did throw a touchdown pass, but he also threw for just 64 yards. He has a middle-of-the-road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, but the Bucs should lean very heavily on their ground game again this week.

The Panthers enter Thursday night with the league's worst run defense, which bodes well for Josh Jacobs' managers. However, Green Bay has also struggled against the run this season and has surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs.

Chuba Hubbard had a disappointing outing in Week 7, as the Bucs boast a strong run defense, and Carolina fell behind early. He should bounce back against the Packers, though, with the potential for a top-10 scoring performance.

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

J.K. Dobbins might remain the Denver Broncos' starter in title, but he's rapidly falling behind in the rotation. RJ Harvey is establishing himself as the top receiving back, and rookie Jonah Coleman looked like the best ball-carrier on the roster during last week's return from injury.

Dobbins will be hard to trust moving forward, and it's impossible to trust him against the Kansas City Chiefs. Kansas City has surrendered the eighth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Start: Stefon Diggs, Washington Commanders

Washington Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs was a bit inconsistent as the team's No. 2 receiver, but with Terry McLaurin out for the year, he's now Jayden Daniels' top target. He recorded 16.4 fantasy points against a good San Francisco 49ers defense in his last game, and he'll face a fading Philadelphia Eagles defense this week.

Philadelphia has now surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing receivers. The Eagles will undoubtedly focus on trying to slow Diggs, but a high target share gives him a high floor.

While Diggs has become Washington's new No. 1 receiver, A.J. Brown was supposed to replace Diggs as the New England Patriots' top target. However, he's struggled to develop chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye and has been a sizeable disappointment instead.

While Brown will probably break out of his funk at some point this season, it's unlikely to happen against the Miami Dolphins. Teams have largely attacked Miami's defense on the ground, which has led to the Dolphins surrendering the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs.

Start: T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings

Any managers in need of a bye-week fill-in at tight end should see if T.J. Hockenson is available. The Vikings pass-catcher is rostered in just 57 percent of leagues and has arguably the top matchup of Week 8.

Minnesota's offense is still trying to find a rhythm, but Hockenson should match or exceed last week's 13.5-point performance. No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing tight ends than the Lions.

Panthers tight end Darren Waller has had some solid outings as a streamer this season, and he's coming off a 12-point performance. However, he's likely to disappoint in fantasy on Thursday night.

While the Packers have been susceptible to the run, they've been quite stout against opposing tight ends. In fact, no team has surrendered fewer fantasy points to the position this season.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Khalil Mack's Top Trade Landing Spots After Jeffery Simmons to Bears Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: As big names continue to fly off the board ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, Los Angeles Chargers pass-rusher Khalil Mack remains among the top players who could be available.
articles.body:
As big names continue to fly off the board ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, Los Angeles Chargers pass-rusher Khalil Mack remains among the top players who could be available.

One team thought to be a suitor for Mack is the Chicago Bears, but they made a blockbuster deal on Thursday, agreeing to send first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, plus a 2027 fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The Simmons trade came two days after the Indianapolis Colts dealt defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.

With the Chargers sitting at 0-6, a Mack trade seems like a strong possibility, and he should garner plenty of interest now that some of the other top trade targets are off the board.

Here is a look at three teams that could make a strong push for Mack ahead of the deadline.

Despite the acquisition of Simmons, the Bears may not necessarily be out of the running for Mack.

Last weekend, NFL insider Jay Glazer appeared on Fox NFL Sunday (h/t SI.com's Mike Moraitis ) and said the Bears had contacted the Chargers to inquire about Mack.

Glazer added that he expected the Bears to be "really aggressive when it comes to the trade deadline."

Although they traded a lot of draft capital for Simmons, the Bears still have their second- and third-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft, as well as the Atlanta Falcons' fifth-rounder.

On top of that, Mack is already quite familiar with Chicago, having played for the Bears from 2018 to 2021. During that time, he was a three-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro.

The Bears are known for their offense, but adding Mack alongside another defensive difference-maker in Simmons would make them one of the most complete teams in the NFC.

The Buffalo Bills are arguably the worst defensive team in the NFL, but they are Super Bowl contenders nonetheless thanks to quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook and the offense.

Buffalo ranks 31st in the NFL in total defense and 30th in scoring defense, as well as tied for 22nd in sacks.

While an edge rusher doesn't seem like the biggest need on the Bills' defense with Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb in starting roles, adding a veteran like Mack—who has three sacks in six games this season—wouldn't hurt.

Mack has been linked to the Bills at various times over the years, but Buffalo was never able to acquire or sign him.

The speculation was likely born partially from the fact that Mack played his college football at the University at Buffalo where he established himself as arguably the greatest player in the history of the program.

Although they are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the best record in the AFC, there is little doubt that the Bills need to make a move or two on defense to bolster their Super Bowl chances, and adding Mack would likely help in a significant way.

Just as it has so many times in recent years, the battle for AFC supremacy this season could come down to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills.

With that in mind, acquiring Mack would serve two purposes for the Chiefs, as it would help their defense, while also blocking the Bills from making a move to improve their defense.

The Chiefs have the No. 2 scoring defense in the NFL this season, allowing just 17.2 points per game, but they haven't put much heat on the quarterback.

Their eight sacks are tied for the second-fewest in the league, and they don't have any players on the roster with more than one sack.

Starting edge rushers George Karlaftis and Felix Anudike-Uzomah have combined for just two sacks, which is nowhere near good enough for a Super Bowl contender.

Mack would instantly become the Chiefs' best pass-rusher, and he would give opposing offenses someone they have to game plan for.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ retirement timeline takes a surprising turn as Chiefs trainer reveals his 10 Super Bowl goal
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has a big goal for his NFL career, and it could decide when he finally walks away from football.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has a big goal for his NFL career, and it could decide when he finally walks away from football. His longtime trainer, Jeff Christensen, says the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback once told him that he would consider retiring after winning 10 Super Bowls. Mahomes has already won three championships, but according to Christensen, his focus remains on becoming the greatest quarterback in NFL history rather than making more money.Jeff Christensen explains Patrick Mahomes’ retirement plan and 10 Super Bowl goalSpeaking on Fearless with Jason Whitlock on Thursday, Christensen shared a conversation he had with Mahomes when the quarterback was a rookie in 2017. He asked the young player about his “get out” number, meaning the point at which he would feel ready to leave football behind.Christensen explained that some players claim money does not matter to them, but their attitude toward the game can change after they sign big contracts. Mahomes, however, gave him an answer that stood out.“Patrick said, ‘My get out is the wins when I win my 10th Super Bowl,’” Christensen recalled.The answer showed that Mahomes had set a clear target for his career from an early age. Instead of naming a salary or a financial goal that would convince him to retire, he pointed to winning championships. His trainer believes that ambition has continued to guide his choices as his career has moved forward.Christensen also remembered telling Mahomes in July 2017 that he had the ability to become the greatest quarterback ever. He said he saw something special in the young player and later shared that view with Matt Kafka before the Chiefs traded Alex Smith.“He just had it,” Christensen said.He also praised Mahomes for staying true to what he said he wanted to achieve. “He does not care about money. He wants to be the greatest. And so his action plan is exactly on schedule.”Christensen’s comments describe how he sees Mahomes’ approach to football, rather than confirming when the quarterback will retire. Mahomes has not announced a retirement date, and winning 10 Super Bowls remains a goal, not a confirmed outcome.Patrick Mahomes has three Super Bowl wins as Chiefs quarterbackMahomes has already won three Super Bowls with Kansas City and earned three Super Bowl MVP awards. His first championship came in Super Bowl LIV, when the Chiefs defeated the San Francisco 49ers. He later led Kansas City to further titles, building a record that puts him among the most successful quarterbacks of his era.He also became the youngest quarterback to win both the regular-season MVP award and the Super Bowl MVP award in the same season, achieving the feat during the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIV campaign.However, his latest career goal comes as Kansas City works through challenges on the field. Mahomes recently addressed reports of a disagreement with offensive lineman Josh Simmons during a team meeting with head coach Andy Reid. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, he said the situation had not taken his attention away from the team’s work.“Stuff like that doesn’t really bother me because I’m so in the moment, in the team,” Mahomes said. “We’ve had the right conversations now. We’re moving in the right direction.”Mahomes also explained why difficult discussions can matter inside a team. “You have to be able to have tough conversations so that you can have better conversations going forward,” he said.Simmons has not played this season because of a back issue, while undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started in his absence. Simmons could return from injured reserve in Week 11 against the Arizona Cardinals on November 22.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor on possibly being traded: 'Hopefully that day may not come, but I can't control that'
articles.summary: Taylor confirmed he has not requested a trade out of Indianapolis.
articles.body:
Jonathan Taylor confirmed Thursday he has not requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts, but acknowledged the situation is out of his control.

"I haven't heard anything," Taylor told reporters Thursday via FOX59's Mike Chappell. "I can't control that, obviously. Like you guys know, I'm proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. Similar to Quenton [Nelson] and [DeForest Buckner], they were proud to wear the horseshoe, they were proud to be here. But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. Hopefully that day may not come, but I can't control that.

"The only thing that I can control is rallying these guys in the locker room, helping us put together a great plan and executing a great plan for Jacksonville because it's a division game and they're licking their chops right now. They think they're going to kick us while we're down and that has to be the point of emphasis."

Taylor's comments come after guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner were dealt earlier this week and following reports that wide receiver Josh Downs has requested to be traded .

Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon reportedly does not want to move Taylor as the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaches. But considering the team is 2-5 and in the midst of a fire sale, interest in the All-Pro running back would certainly be high if he is made available.

"Those are hypothetical things right now," head coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday when asked if Taylor had asked out . "I know there's stuff floating around out there, but JT's on our football team."

The 27-year-old Taylor, who said he has met with Irsay-Gordon about his future, is in his seventh NFL season, all with the Colts. He signed a two-year, $44 millon extension in August with $39 million in guaranteed money. The extension runs through the 2028 season with his salary cap hit at $16.2 million this season, $21 million in 2027 and just under $23 million in 2028, according to Over the Cap .

Taylor has rushed for at least 1,100 yards in four of his six NFL seasons and has just under 600 yards through seven games this season.

articles.title: Grading Jeffery Simmons Blockbuster NFL Trade Between Titans and Bears
articles.summary: The NFL's November 10 trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and we've seen several significant moves this week alone. Another massive domino dropped on Thursday, as the Tennessee Titans agreed to send star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
The NFL's November 10 trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and we've seen several significant moves this week alone. Another massive domino dropped on Thursday, as the Tennessee Titans agreed to send star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Titans will receive first- and fourth-round picks in 2027, along with a 2028 first-rounder in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

While we've already seen notable players like Marvin Harrison Jr., Quenton Nelson, and DeForest Buckner traded in-season, this deal marks the first real blockbuster of the fall. The Titans are getting a very sizeable haul, while Chicago gets a four-time Pro Bowler who is one of the top front-line defenders in the game.

The trade raises questions about what's next for the 1-6 Titans while making clear the Bears' intentions to chase the Super Bowl in 2026. Let's take a closer look at the trade, Simmons' outlook, and what the deal means for the defensive standout, the Bears, and the Titans.

Let's make one thing clear. Moving Simmons may not sit well with fans, and it probably won't be appreciated by head coach Robert Saleh, who has been trying to build up a defense capable of making Tennessee competitive. From a franchise-building perspective, though, it's a win for the Titans and general manager Mike Borgonzi.

The reality is that the Titans haven't been competitive since moving on from coach Mike Vrabel following the 2023 season. They have won just seven games since the start of 2024, and things haven't really been trending upward in 2026.

Tennessee currently ranks 26th in total defense, 32nd in total offense, and has only defeated the Indianapolis Colts—who began their own fire sale this week by dealing Nelson and Buckner.

To make matters worse, the Titans still don't know what they have in 2025 first overall pick Cam Ward. The Miami product has shown occasional flashes of franchise-QB upside but hasn't made the sort of second-year jump that Tennessee expected from him.

Despite having new support pieces like receiver Wan'Dale Robinson and rookie wideout Carnell Tate , Ward has actually seen a dip in efficiency. After posting a QB rating of 80.2 as a rookie, Ward currently holds a rating of just 73.8.

Borgonzi and Co. may soon have to decide whether to stick with Ward or consider dipping into next year's draft class. And if they stick with Ward in 2027, they may again reevaluate the situation in 2028.

By flipping Simmons for two first-round picks, the Titans have given themselves flexibility in each of the next two drafts. Next April, the extra draft capital could allow Tennessee to further upgrade Ward's supporting cast or provide the pieces needed to secure the QB prospect of its choice.

That's assuming the Titans don't continue to lose and wind up with the No. 1 overall pick for the second time in three years.

It's also a strong return for Simmons, who will turn 30 in the spring. While Simmons just signed an extension in June that runs through 2030, the trade isn't financially crippling for Tennessee, either. According to Spotrac , the Titans will absorb dead-cap hits of $14.1 million in 2026 and $21.2 million in 2027 to facilitate the deal.

Those are substantial cap hits, but they represent a reasonable price for two premier draft selections when the Titans lead the league in available cap space.

There's obviously no guarantee that either of those first-round picks will help deliver a player of Simmons' caliber, but betting on the future makes perfect sense for the Titans at this juncture.

The timing was right for the Titans to trade Simmons, and the timing was right for Chicago to make a bold move. The Bears appear to have their long-term coach-quarterback pairing in Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson. They also have several potent offensive pieces with which to work.

Despite losing Williams for a stretch to a hamstring injury, Chicago ranks third in total offense and eighth in scoring while owning a 5-2 record. Johnson believes that there's still room for offensive growth, too.

"There's a lot of room for improvement in the running game and in the passing game as well," Johnson told reporters (h/t Chris Pownall of FanSided). "I'm not going to divulge, but there's, I think, there's a lot more to be had."

What the Bears have lacked dating back to the start of last season is a truly dominant defense.

Chicago has been quite adept at creating turnovers, limiting third-down conversions, and keeping points off the board this season, which has allowed the defense to rank eighth overall and ninth in points allowed. However, the Bears rank just 23rd in yards per carry allowed and 31st in net yards per pass attempt allowed. A team with realistic Super Bowl aspirations has to be more efficient on a down-by-down basis.

Adding Simmons will help the Bears be exactly that. A first-team All-Pro in 2025, Simmons is a top-tier run defender and a disruptive interior pass rusher. He has recorded 15 sacks since the start of last season, has six tackles for loss this season, and is currently graded 12th overall among interior defenders by Pro Football Focus .

Simmons might be exactly the missing piece that Chicago needs to catch the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North.

This wasn't just a swing by GM Ryan Poles for the current season, either. Signed through 2030, Simmons can anchor Chicago's defensive front for the foreseeable future.

Now, there is some risk involved here. The Bears gave up premium picks for a player who will turn 30 in the offseason, and the risk of an age-related decline is real. However, we've seen several defensive tackles play at a high level well into their mid-30s, and the price for Simmons may not be quite as high as it would seem at first blush.

The Cincinnati Bengals' offseason trade for Dexter Lawrence serves as a good comparison. To acquire the 28-year-old defensive tackle, Cincinnati surrendered the 10th overall pick, a draft slot that is expected to yield a blue-chip prospect. Barring a massive letdown, the two first-round picks Chicago is trading for Simmons will fall near the end of the draft order.

If the Bears are able to reach the divisional round in each of the next two years, they'll actually be giving up less in traditional trade value than the Bengals gave up for Lawrence.

Thursday's trade may have come as a surprise to Simmons, who stated he had no information on an impending deal.

"I haven't heard anything from my agent, I haven't heard anything from this organization. As far as I know, I am going to be here," Simmons told reporters on Wednesday, per Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official website.

If it was a surprise to Simmons, it was likely a pleasant one.

The 19th overall pick in the 2019 draft, Simmons did experience some team success with the Titans. After reaching the AFC Championship Game as a rookie, though, it's been all downhill. Tennessee lost playoff games in 2020 and 2021, and Simmons hasn't experienced a winning season since.

Simmons has been paid handsomely by the Titans, and he currently ranks third among interior defenders in terms of annual salary . However, his "success" in Tennessee has been limited to sizeable paychecks and individual accolades. That should change in Chicago.

The Bears appear poised to at least be playoff-relevant for the next several years, and it's not outlandish to view Chicago as a legitimate Super Bowl contender now—especially with Simmons joining the defense.

Presumably, Simmons will play alongside Grady Jarrett in Dennis Allen's defense, giving Chicago a very formidable defensive front. This should help the Bears maintain a top-10 defense while putting more pressure on opposing quarterbacks trying to match points with Williams and the Bears.

This trade allows Simmons to leave arguably the NFL's most directionless franchises for one that is ascending. Simmons will finally get the chance to experience team success again, while potentially putting up even better numbers and racking up more individual awards.

From both short- and long-term perspectives, it's hard to envision Simmons landing in a better situation.

Simmons had been a subject of somewhat regular trade speculation with Tennessee struggling to contend. Its last playoff trip was in 2021.

Both parties seemingly put the issue to bed by striking a bargain on a three-year, $105.8 million extension in June.

Simmons said at the time that "Tennessee has become a second home for me," and he was "focused on helping this team get back to competing for championships."

Given he's under contract through his age-33 season, it was reasonable to assume he could spend the remainder of his career in Nashville.

Things are rarely that straightforward in sports, though.

Borgonzi had to operate in the Titans' best interests, and two first-round picks is a massive haul for Simmons.

It's on the front office and coaching staff to make the most of that draft capital. In theory, the first-rounders should yield more value to a rebuilding team than what Simmons would've provided.

The 29-year-old has been in the NFL long enough to understand the business side of the game. Still, it's a little jarring when you're the one who's being unexpectedly shipped out.

articles.title: Grading the trade: Bears closer to a Super Bowl with Simmons, but the cost was steep
articles.summary: The Bears added a scheme wrecker who could significantly upgrade their defensive front. The Titans added significant draft resources.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears swung the biggest pre-deadline trade yet by acquiring Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons .

The Bears reportedly will send first-round draft picks in 2027 and 2028, along with a fourth-round selection in 2027, to the Titans for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder.

Simmons, 29, is a four-time Pro Bowl selection and is coming off a first-team All-Pro season in 2025, earning him a three-year, $105.8 million extension in the offseason.

This deal significantly alters the paths for both franchises in the short and long terms. Who got the better end of the trade? Let's dive into the details.

Bears take big swing for the fences, but at a high cost

The Bears appeared serious about upgrading their talent prior to the trade deadline, with reported interest in the Indianapolis Colts' DeForest Buckner prior to him being traded to the San Francisco 49ers . With the Simmons deal, the Bears made an even bigger plunge — and the price tag reflected that.

By sending their next two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder next year, the Bears are shipping out major assets the next two years. This trade sends a clear signal that the Bears are going for it all this season.

Simmons remains in the peak of his career, having just turned 29 at the start of training camp, and should have several prime years remaining. He's played a whopping 425 of the Titans' 490 defensive snaps (86.7%), which is just about as high a percentage as you'll see for an interior player.

The Titans used him as a one-gap penetrator but he is capable of lining up at just about any technique up front. He's a high-motor rusher and an elite run stopper who still demands and draws double teams at a high rate. In his Week 6 game against the Colts, Simmons faced multiple blockers often yet finished with a game-high seven pressures.

This should be a huge addition for defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's front, which has been undermanned. Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street have taken the majority of the interior snaps, with rookie Jordan van den Berg also filling in. The results have been mediocre.

The Bears' defensive rankings might look impressive on the surface (eighth in yards allowed, 10th in points), but on a per-play basis, they're ranked close to the bottom in several categories. What has saved the Bears is an offense that's possessing the ball for an average of 35:30 — more than three minutes per game ahead of the next-closest team.

Chicago's schedule is brutal down the stretch, and they're going to face some impressive offenses, including two games left vs. the Lions, plus tough tests against the Jaguars and Bills. Simmons and some other defensive reinforcements might be enough to stabilize things up front.

The Bears recently got Montez Sweat back from suspension, and he'll certainly benefit from Simmons' arrival. It's a significant stretch for Sweat, who has a major cap hit next season and must finish strong to prove his value. The team also got Shemar Turner back recently and figures to get Dayo Odeyingbo back eventually. With a full cast, this line could turn from a below-average group on the whole to a possible team strength.

Value-wise, this is close to as much compensation as you'll see moved for a defensive player. But if the Bears make a Super Bowl run, the price very well could make the move a smart one.

Titans gain terrific draft value for Simmons

It's never easy to deal away an elite talent such as Simmons, especially for a team like Tennessee, which has only so many high-value players. There's a reason the Titans paid him handsomely in the offseason: Simmons is an elite defender coming off a career year.

He's also played well amid the Titans' struggles this season, in spite of extra blocking attention on many snaps. Offenses came into most games against them with a plan for Simmons. Now the Titans are losing that, a significant blow to defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh.

But assuming Saleh is back next season, the Titans will have vast resources to use on upgrading the roster. They're 1-6 and headed toward a top-10 (and likely top-five draft pick next spring). The Bears' pick is expected to be lower, likely in the bottom third of Round 1, but they will now have six choices in the first four rounds and ample flexibility to target whatever they want.

With Cam Ward off to another uneven start, that could even include quarterback — this season or next. Landing the 2028 first-rounder as well gives the Titans a two-year window with major assets to protect themselves in case Ward isn't the QB they thought he was when they drafted him first overall. If he does pan out, those picks can be allocated to other spots, including to a defense that just lost a major enforcer.

It likely would have been too hard for general manager Mike Borgonzi to turn down this offer. He likely had multiple teams bidding and was able to get the Bears up to the price level they were comfortable with. Adding a fourth-rounder in 2027 for a 2028 fifth was a nice sweetener.

The Titans are facing a multi-year rebuild, and this was the best way to help starting toward that effort. They have more needs today than they did yesterday, and picks are merely lottery tickets, but this felt like a deal Borgonzi had to make.

articles.title: Study finds roughly 75% of deceased NFL players had at least some degree of CTE brain disease
articles.summary: A study of more than 2,300 deceased NFL players estimates roughly 75% had CTE, the degenerative brain disease linked to repeated head trauma in football.
articles.body: A recent study found that roughly 75% of deceased NFL players had at least some case of CTE. Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a progressive, degenerative brain disease linked to repeated head impacts rather than a single injury, according to the Mayo Clinic. The study from Boston University researchers consisted of more than 2,300 deceased former players aged 80 or older who died between 2008 and 2023, nearly 400 of whom were donors. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Out of the 396 who donated their brains to research, 93.5% of them were diagnosed. Researchers estimated that former NFL players with clear cognitive symptoms were roughly five times more likely to donate their brains than those without such symptoms. Donors also died younger on average - 67 years old compared to almost 75. CTE can only be diagnosed after death and is identified in four stages, with stage 4 being the worst. "Many cases may have been early stage at the time of death and possibly symptom free," the study noted. The study also estimated that 27.2% of the players had a history of all-cause dementia during life, but it did not conclude whether dementia was caused by CTE. JUSTIN TUCKER SIGNS WITH CHIEFS AFTER SERVING 10-GAME SUSPENSION OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS: REPORTS A study released in August found that at least 1 in 4 people who have played in the NFL might expect to end up with CTE at some point in their lives. The symptoms found in those with CTE include memory loss, mood swings, erratic behavioral actions and more. While the disease was first found in boxers, it has become associated with football players in this modern era due to the repeated blows to the head sustained on every snap of the ball. It has, however, also been found in athletes participating in hockey, rugby and other sports. But its connection to football became public when beloved players like Junior Seau, Mike Webster, Frank Gifford and others were diagnosed with CTE after their deaths. Webster was dubbed "Patient Zero" after Dr. Bennet Omalu examined his brain and became the first to diagnose an NFL player with CTE, jump-starting a concussion crisis within the game. There were a total of 538 evaluations and 26 medical timeouts as well. OutKick's Scott Thompson contributed to this report.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' International Schedule Proposal Reportedly Has No Support From NFL Owners
articles.summary: NFL owners are reportedly not behind the "international week" idea recently proposed by Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
NFL owners are reportedly not behind the "international week" idea recently proposed by Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

According to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, there is "virtually no support" among NFL owners and management for Rodgers' suggestion of playing 16 international games in a single week.

One source told Maske, "You'd be competing against yourself. It's a nonsensical concept."

Following the Steelers' 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints last weekend in Paris, Rodgers took some shots at the manner in which the NFL deploys its international games before telling reporters that he would support one week of international games with an added bye week.

"There was talk about doing a week—an international week—where you had games in 16 different places and you just added an extra bye week. So you play 16 regular-season [weeks], you have two bye weeks—one of those weeks would've been an international week.

"I think it would've been phenomenal for the game. Now, the owners wanted to push for 17 games for the extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety, but it would've been nice."

Per Maske, the NFL and its players "never discussed" the idea of an international week during collective bargaining discussions in 2020, and it "won't be considered" moving forward.

Since 2005, the NFL has played international games annually outside of the 2020 season, which was impacted by COVID-19.

While most of those international games have taken place in London, it has expanded to include Mexico, France, Germany, Spain, Ireland, Brazil and Australia.

A record nine international games will be played this season, and the league figures to continue expanding the slate in the years to come.

articles.title: Adam Schefter Makes Feelings Clear on Packers’ Jordan Love
articles.summary: ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said Thursday on Get Up that Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love has not proven he is elite.Schefter added that no quart...
articles.body:
ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said Thursday on Get Up that Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love has not proven he is elite.

Schefter added that no quarterback proves elite status in October.

Love ranks second in the NFL with 1,958 passing yards through seven games. He has thrown 13 touchdowns and five interceptions while completing 59.8 percent of his passes.

The Packers sit at 4-3 and last in the NFC North after a 20-17 loss at the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Love finished 27 of 45 for 274 yards with two touchdowns and one interception in that game.

Schefter credited Love for performing despite major offensive shortcomings.

"Now listen, when you have a run game that is not produced and you've got an offensive line that doesn't protect, and you've got all those issues, that falls on the quarterback," Schefter said . "And the fact that Jordan Love has stepped up proves, as Taylor says, he's a really good quarterback."

A fellow panelist noted he had called Love a hell of a quarterback rather than simply a really good one.

"But I don't think that a quarterback proves he's elite in October, with all due respect," Schefter said. "That's not when you're proving you're elite. Jordan Love is going to prove he's elite. In January. In February."

"He could be, as you say, a hell of a quarterback. And he's a hell of a quarterback," Schefter continued. "But nobody's showing their elite right now in October."

His only postseason win came in a 48-32 Wild Card victory at Dallas in January 2024, when he threw three touchdown passes. Green Bay lost to San Francisco the next week.

The Packers later fell 22-10 at Philadelphia in January 2025 after Love threw three interceptions. They lost 31-27 at Chicago in the Wild Card round on Jan. 10.

Green Bay ranks last in the NFL in rushing at 59.9 yards per game. The team has managed just 419 total rushing yards in seven contests.

The Packers signed Love to a four-year, $220 million extension in July 2024 that included a $75 million signing bonus.

The Carolina Panthers visit Lambeau Field for Thursday Night Football. Kickoff is set for 7:15 p.m. CT.

Love has produced volume through the air while the ground game has lagged. His 90.3 passer rating ranks outside the top tier early in the season.

Schefter's comments center on the difference between strong regular season numbers and proven postseason success. The Packers remain in the playoff picture despite the division standing.

articles.title: ESPN Analysts Say Minnesota Vikings Player Has ‘50%’ Chance of Being Traded Soon
articles.summary: The Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and while several NFC teams have been active, the undefeated Minnesota […]
articles.body:
The Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and while several NFC teams have been active, the undefeated Minnesota Vikings have stood pat. Yet, the belief is that first-year general manager Nolan Teasley has been actively involved in trade negotiations; he just hasn't executed a deal yet.

Though, just because the Vikings have remained dormant, it doesn't necessarily mean that a trade isn't coming. In fact, some analysts pretty much expect at least one deal from the Vikings. However, in this case, it's because they think a current Vikings player will be traded in the next two weeks.

ESPN Suggests Jauan Jennings Has a High Chance of Being Traded From Minnesota Vikings

Vikings fans are pretty focused on the possibility of adding a star running back to help jumpstart the offense, such as Jonathan Taylor , Breece Hall, or even Saquon Barkley. Others would like to see the NFL's best defense get even better with the addition of another pressure-generating DT or a rotational edge rusher.

Yet, the trade that ESPN's analysts find most likely is one that actually subtracts Jauan Jennings from the roster. How likely is a Jennings trade before the deadline? ESPN puts the odds at 50% .

"The Vikings' free agent addition is not a focal point of the offense and is considered a trade candidate leaguewide. But he did catch two passes for 34 yards Sunday against the Colts for a Minnesota passing game that's not exactly thriving right now. Jennings, who's on a one-year deal, could prove a low-cost option for teams looking to add to their receiver room. The 49ers are an obvious fit." Jeremy Fowler on Jauan Jennings

"The Vikings' free agent addition is not a focal point of the offense and is considered a trade candidate leaguewide. But he did catch two passes for 34 yards Sunday against the Colts for a Minnesota passing game that's not exactly thriving right now. Jennings, who's on a one-year deal, could prove a low-cost option for teams looking to add to their receiver room. The 49ers are an obvious fit."

While a reunion with the San Francisco 49ers seems like the most obvious fit for the physical receiver with an affinity for run blocking, ESPN also lists the WR-needy Los Angeles Rams and Atlanta Falcons as other potential landing spots.

With Jennings signed to a one-year deal but really only offering production as a run-blocker, it makes sense for the Vikings to consider offers that give the 29-year-old a better opportunity to produce as a pass-catcher. Whether those offers materialize remains to be seen, and the Vikings are still hopeful that the veteran will continue to be a bigger part of their offense, as seen with his best game yet with his new team in Week 7.

Some out there even think the Vikings could send Jennings back to San Francisco while acquiring another player from Kyle Shanahan's team . While it's unclear what will happen between now and the NFL trade deadline on the 10th, there's a strong sense the Vikings will do something , and it's very possible that trading Jennings is part of the plan.
