articles.title: Titans GM revealed a really surprising fact about the Jeffery Simmons trade
articles.summary: The Titans treated Jeffery Simmons in a stunning way before dealing him to the Bears.
articles.body:
In his eight-year NFL career, Jeffery Simmons has distinguished himself as the kind of dynamic player a franchise keeps all communication channels open for. Even despite the Tennessee Titans ' losing in recent years, Simmons was one of their biggest champions. This, on top of his play as a disruptive, perennial All-Pro defensive tackle. So you'd think the Titans' organizational leadership would, at the very least, tell the superstar defender he was about to be traded from a place he didn't want to leave.

After the Titans traded Simmons away to the Chicago Bears — in turn, giving Caleb Williams an understandable jolt of excitement — the team's general manager, Mike Borgonzi, revealed a stunning tidbit about the blockbuster deal. Even despite Simmons' status as the Titans' clear franchise player, he didn't find out about the monster trade ... until it was done .

That's right. In fact, when Bears general manager Ryan Poles called Borgonzi to initiate trade talks on Wednesday night, Borgonzi said he wasted no time putting everything into motion once the two teams agreed upon the trade compensation. This meant that Simmons was on the outside looking in on the process the entire time as Tennessee dealt him away for the princely sum of two first-round draft picks. Phew.

I don't know that that's how I would personally treat a departing star player, even if it is to a Super Bowl contender. The least Borgonzi could've done is give Simmons and his agent a heads-up text. But Borgonzi clearly must have felt that informing Simmons of the deal would've thrown a snag into the deal, so he wasted no time moving on it:

Even if the outcome is probably the best for both parties — Simmons will get to play for championships in his prime, while the Titans get more assets to build around Cam Ward — that is cold-blooded business, dearest readers. I think all of us already knew this, but it goes to show you that loyalty only goes so far in the NFL. We'll have to see how Simmons responds to this emotional change, if at all, as he sets his sights on Chicago.

articles.title: Starts and sits for fantasy football ahead of Week 8
articles.summary: Here are our top starts and sits for NFL fantasy football in Week 8, including starting Dak Prescott and benching Tony Pollard.
articles.body:
Fantasy football is a mess. Multiple running backs went off last week, most notably Tony Pollard and Quidshon Judkins, who were probably on a lot of people's benches last week. Kickers were deciding games with missed field goals. The Dallas Cowboys' offense finally came back, returning some of their players to fantasy relevance.

Bye weeks will certainly play a factor once again with the Houston Texans, New York Giants, New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers on bye. Luckily, there are some under-the-radar prospects who can be in your lineup this week to fill in for your players on bye.

So, who should and should not be in your fantasy lineup? Here are our starts and sits for Week 8:

Photos from Bears' statement win over the Patriots in Week 7

Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys finally got things back on track offensively in their win over the Philadelphia Eagles. He threw three touchdowns, his most since Week 2 against the Washington Commanders. Now, Prescott gets one of the best matchups he could ask for against the Arizona Cardinals, who are giving up a lot of points to quarterbacks in fantasy. Bet on another multi-touchdown game for Prescott.

Sit: QB Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams

While Dallas is getting back on track, the Los Angeles Rams are not. Davante Adams will be out for a while, leaving a large gap in Los Angeles' offense. Matthew Stafford actually has multiple touchdowns in the past three games, but his fantasy production over the past two weeks has been poor because of his lack of passing yards. He even had a bad game against the Cardinals. This week, he faces one of the better defenses in the NFL. Despite their winless record, the Los Angeles Chargers have been a problem for quarterbacks in fantasy. It may be a good week to put Stafford on your bench and stream an option from the waiver wire.

Usually, split backfields hurt both running backs in fantasy. However, the Los Angeles Rams are currently an exception, with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum getting decent points. Furthermore, the Chargers may hold quarterbacks to few points, but the same does not apply to running backs. In fact, they are actually a good matchup for running backs in fantasy, so Corum should hit his production at the very least in this game.

Even though he just put up three touchdowns last week, Tony Pollard should be on the bench. That is not close to how Pollard usually performs. In fact, he only had one rushing touchdown and had not put up 100 rushing yards in a game until last week. Now Pollard is facing one of the best run defenses in the NFL. He can only go down from his performance last week and it is probably going to be a large decline.

Start: WR Omar Cooper Jr., New York Jets

Omar Cooper Jr is someone who has flown under the radar this season, in part because he missed time due to an injury. However, in both of his full games this season, he has over 100 receiving yards and a touchdown. His target share is also decent despite the Jets also having Garrett Wilson and having Geno Smith at quarterback. Especially if you have a receiver or two on bye, Cooper is a great option with high upside in a decent matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Sit: WR A.J. Brown, New England Patriots

First, A.J. Brown popped up on the injury report again with knee and ankle injuries. But more importantly, he has not developed chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye and it is impacting his fantasy performance. In the last two games, he has been targeted 16 times. However, he only has six receptions for 75 yards. Furthermore, despite the Miami Dolphins' record, they are also generally a bad matchup for receivers. A.J. Brown needs to stay on the bench.

Start: TE T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings

T.J. Hockenson is a streaky tight end. But, there is good reason to believe he will have a good game against the Detroit Lions. Simply put, Detroit is terrible against tight ends this season. In just six games, they have given up 602 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns to tight ends. Minnesota will have a plan to exploit the Lions' defense with Hockenson given their performance this season and it will result in a lot of fantasy points.

On the other side of this game, the Vikings have been shutting down tight ends all season. In six games, they have only given up 233 receiving yards against tight ends and are one of two teams in the NFL that have not allowed a tight end to catch a touchdown pass. Especially after having only one reception last week, Sam LaPorta needs to stay on the bench this week.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Injury Update: Knee Issue Has Patriots WR 'Up in the Air' for Week 8 Game
articles.summary: Brown missed Thursday's practice with a knee issue in addition to his lingering ankle injury, leaving his status for Sunday's game against Miami uncertain.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is dealing with another injury concern ahead of Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Brown was absent from Thursday's practice after a knee issue flared up, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The veteran was also listed on Wednesday's injury report with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday's game uncertain.

The latest development adds another question to Brown's health as he continues working his way back from the ankle injury that sidelined him for four games earlier this season.

A.J. Brown's Injury History Raises Concerns for Patriots

Brown suffered a high ankle sprain during New England's season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, forcing him to miss four games. The Patriots activated him from injured reserve ahead of their Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets.

The receiver has appeared in New England's last two games, but his production has been limited as he works back into the offense. Brown recorded three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets against the Jets before finishing with three receptions for 48 yards on six targets in the Patriots' Week 7 loss to the Chicago Bears.

Brown also acknowledged Wednesday that his ankle has not fully recovered.

"Yeah, sometimes, you know, I see it, and sometimes, I'm pushing through," Brown said via NFL.com . "But none of that stuff even matters. I'm out here, so I'm going."

The knee issue now gives New England another injury to monitor as it prepares for Miami.

Patriots Need A.J. Brown Against Dolphins

Brown's availability is especially important for a Patriots offense dealing with injuries at wide receiver. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs also have been unavailable, increasing the importance of Brown's presence in the passing game.

New England will face Miami on the road Sunday as it looks to rebound from its loss to Chicago. Brown's ability to practice over the remainder of the week will be an important factor in determining whether he can suit up.

The Patriots have not ruled Brown out, but his status remains uncertain following Thursday's absence. New England's subsequent injury reports should provide a clearer picture of whether the wide receiver will be available for Week 8.

articles.title: Caleb Williams says he'll continue to wear unathorized cleats during games despite $12,000 fines
articles.summary: Caleb Williams risks fines every game if he continues to display an "unauthorized logo" on the field.
articles.body:
How important are Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' new cleats? Important enough that the star is willing to pay roughly $12,000 every game to keep wearing them.

Williams, who was fined $11,941 for displaying an "unauthorized logo" on his cleats during the team's Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons, said Wednesday he intends to keep wearing the cleats the rest of the season.

Those cleats, which are made by a company called Caddix, were designed with the intention of reducing ACL and ankle injuries thanks to the way their studs rotate and release on a surface.

Problem is, Caddix does not have a deal with the NFL. Because of that, the company's logo cannot be displayed by players during games.

Williams, who does not have an endorsement deal with Caddix, spoke highly of the cleats Wednesday, and said he intended to continue wearing them because he believes in the science behind the cleats.

"I'm huge into my body. I'm huge into trying to stay on the field. I'm huge into trying to be healthy," Williams said. "It's a rough game."

After explaining how the shoes work, Williams said he wants to keep wearing the cleats because he sees the importance of taking some wear and tear off his body during his career.

"Over the course of a long career or over the course of a long year, when you can take some percentage, it can be one, it could be 50, it could be 12, it could be whatever. When you take that percentage off consistently over a period of time, you get to have the chance, a higher chance of being healthy. That's what I focus on. I try to be healthy."

Williams added that his lower body hasn't bothered him as much this season, which partly fueled his decision to keep wearing the cleats.

The quarterback has worn the unauthorized shoes throughout the entire preseason and in both Week 1 and 2 before he went down with a hamstring injury. Thus far, he's only been fined for wearing the Caddix cleats in Week 6. Images from the team's Week 7 game against the New England Patriots also shows Williams wearing the cleats. As of Thursday, he has not received a fine from the NFL, at least not one that's been acknowledged publicly.

Williams is far from the only player to wear Caddix cleats this season. Complex compiled a list of various players who have used the cleats in 2026.

While Williams' fines could rack up quickly if the NFL decides to hammer home the issue, it doesn't sound like the quarterback has to worry about that. Upon hearing of the fine, Caddix's CEO, Jack Rasmussen, has reportedly offered to pay Williams' fines . Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco, who has worn Caddix cleats for a while now, told ESPN he was also willing to pay Williams' fine the next time the NFL comes calling.

articles.summary: A new study has raised fresh concerns about the long-term effects of playing in the NFL.
articles.body: A new study has raised fresh concerns about the long-term effects of playing in the NFL. The study, published in JAMA Network Open, looked at 2,362 former NFL players who died during the 16-year period. Nearly 75% of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts.Scary NFL study reveals nearly 75% of deceased players had a devastating brain diseaseResearchers from Boston University, Mass General Brigham and the Concussion & CTE Foundation worked together to estimate how common the disease was among the group. The findings are concerning because CTE has been linked to repeated blows to the head, something football players can experience throughout their careers. However, researchers stressed that the 74.5% figure is an estimate, not a confirmed diagnosis for every player included in the study.Of the former players included in the study, 387 had donated brains that were examined for CTE. Researchers found signs of the disease in 362 of them, or 93.5%. That is a very high percentage, but there is an important reason why the researchers did not use it as the final figure for all former NFL players.Families may be more likely to donate a player's brain if their loved one experienced memory problems, personality changes or other cognitive symptoms before death. This means that donated brains may not represent every former player who died during the same period.To account for this, the researchers examined additional records and adjusted their calculations to account for differences between players whose brains were donated and those whose brains were not. After making those adjustments, they estimated that 74.5% of all 2,362 deceased former players had CTE-related changes in their brains.Several famous NFL players have been diagnosed with CTE after death. Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez, who died in 2017 at age 27, was found to have Stage 3 CTE. Former San Diego Chargers linebacker Junior Seau, who died in 2012 at age 43, was also diagnosed with CTE after his death.Other notable cases include former Chicago Bears safety Dave Duerson, who died in 2011 at age 50, and former NFL quarterback Ken Stabler, who died in 2015 at age 69. Both were found to have CTE through postmortem brain examinations.What is CTE, and why is it concerning? The study also examined dementia among former playersChronic traumatic encephalopathy, commonly known as CTE, is a progressive brain disease associated with repeated head impacts. It has been found in athletes who participated in contact sports, including American football.The disease is linked to an abnormal buildup of a protein called tau in the brain. Possible symptoms associated with CTE include memory loss, difficulty thinking, mood changes and problems with behavior or judgment. However, not everyone with CTE-related brain changes experiences the same symptoms. Some people may have relatively mild changes, while others may experience more serious problems.Another major challenge is that CTE can currently be confirmed only after death through an examination of brain tissue. Doctors cannot definitively diagnose the disease in a living person using routine medical tests. This also means researchers cannot use the new study to determine how many living NFL players currently have CTE.The researchers looked at dementia as a separate issue and estimated that 27.2% of the former NFL players had a history of dementia during their lifetime. Dementia can affect memory, thinking and a person's ability to manage everyday activities. However, it is not the same as CTE, and the two figures should not be confused.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "I am in tears for such a gift": Travis Kelce's $2 million gift brings hope to families of fallen NYPD officers and firefighters

articles.body: In July 2026, Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift made a charitable contribution that reached far beyond their high-profile wedding celebrations. The couple donated $2 million to Answer The Call, a New York nonprofit that supports families of first responders killed in the line of duty. The gift moved families who have spent years coping with loss, offering financial support and a reminder that their loved ones have not been forgotten. For Kelce, the donation also put the spotlight on how public figures can use major life milestones to support people facing challenges that extend well beyond the sporting world.Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift donate $2 million to Answer The CallThe donation formed part of a wider charitable effort by the newlyweds, who reportedly contributed a combined $26 million to organisations across the United States during their wedding week. Their $2 million gift to Answer The Call stood out for its direct connection to families who lost loved ones while serving New York City.Founded in 1985, Answer The Call provides immediate financial assistance and ongoing stipends to the families of fallen New York City police officers, firefighters, Port Authority police officers and emergency medical services personnel.On July 20, the organisation thanked Kelce and Swift through an Instagram post featuring letters from nine recipients. Their messages showed how the support reaches beyond financial help, offering families comfort and recognition years after tragedy.Valerie Perry, whose husband, William, was a Port Authority police officer, described the lasting impact of the fund. He was shot and killed on December 22, 1980, and his family buried him on Christmas Eve.“Answer the Call has changed my life with our yearly checks, but they have also brought smiles because I feel like my Bill is always remembered, even after all these years,” she said.Perry also expressed her emotional response to the couple's contribution.“Now, to read about your donation? I am in tears for such a gift to all these families that have been through so much.“Prayers for your future together, and God bless both of you for your generosity and your caring souls for doing something so amazing.”Travis Kelce’s wedding donation brings comfort to families of fallen first respondersThe response from recipients highlighted the emotional weight of supporting families who continue to live with the loss of loved ones. For many, such contributions recognise not only their financial needs but also the sacrifices made by the people they lost.Theresa Giammona, whose husband, FDNY Captain Vincent Giammona, died in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, also thanked the couple. She recalled Swift performing at America’s Camp, a summer camp established for children who lost loved ones in the attacks.“My children have been devoted Taylor fans ever since they saw you perform at America’s Camp in 2003,” Giammona said. “What always meant the most to us is that you never forgot the America’s Camp families.”She added: “Thank you for Answering the Call, for your generosity, and most of all, for never forgetting the families you have continued to lift up over the years.”Answer The Call also praised Kelce and Swift for their support, saying: “Taylor and Travis, thank you for your incredible generosity and for standing with the families of fallen New York City first responders,” the organization said on Instagram. “Your gift will make a tangible difference in their lives.”The donation offered a meaningful example of how the couple's wedding celebrations could create opportunities to support others. While Kelce is best known for his NFL career, the contribution placed attention on a different side of his public life. For families who have endured decades of grief, the gift carried a message that their loved ones' service and sacrifice still matter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Colts Trade Rumors Reveal 1 Player Off-Limits in Talks Despite NFL Interest During Fire Sale
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have wasted no time making trades ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 deadline, but there is reportedly one player they will not move.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have wasted no time making trades ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 deadline, but there is reportedly one player they will not move.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Thursday that Indianapolis has no plans on trading defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore and "sees him as a big part of the picture moving forward."

While Garafolo previously reported Adebawore would generate interest if he was made available, he noted the Colts will "surely" look to extend his deal at this point before he becomes a free agent during the upcoming offseason.

Even if Indianapolis plans on holding onto Adebawore, the AFC South team has been at the center of the NFL world leading up to the trade deadline.

It already moved defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers and offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. What's more, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported wide receiver Josh Downs requested a trade.

That's not even getting into running back Jonathan Taylor, who did not request a trade but has been speculated about leading up to the deadline.

He even admitted he knows he doesn't fully control his future:

One thing is clear. It appears the Colts are staring at a rebuilding process after making two notable moves with more potentially to come. That will make their young players and draft capital all the more important, so perhaps it shouldn't come as a surprise they want to keep Adebawore.

After all, he is just 25 years old and will likely have an even bigger role now that Buckner is no longer on the defensive line.

The 2023 fourth-round pick has four sacks in seven games this season, which is already tied for his career high. He also has 17 total tackles and three tackles for loss to go along with eight quarterback hits.

He appears to have turned the corner this season and will now have even more opportunity following the Buckner trade. If he takes advantage of those chances, there could be quite the contract waiting for him.

articles.title: Chiefs Make Harrison Butker Decision After Justin Tucker Addition Amid Kicker's Struggles

articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will stick with Harrison Butker as their kicker despite the 10-year veteran's recent struggles and the addition of Justin Tucker to the practice squad, per comments that special teams coordinator Dave Toub made to reporters on Thursday.

"We're trying to improve and get Butker right," Toub said. "That's what this whole thing is about. He's our kicker. He went 10-for-10 yesterday with Tucker standing right there. It was a windy day. It was 28 miles an hour gusts yesterday. That's a good thing. We're going to keep working it."

Javonte Carries Cowboys Back Into Race 😤

Butker is 11-of-16 on field goals this year, including 2-of-6 from 50 or more yards. He missed attempts from 45 and 58 yards last Sunday evening, when the Chiefs lost on the road to the Seattle Seahawks 20-3.

Butker has been the Chiefs' kicker for five AFC winners and three Super Bowl champions. He's fared quite well over time, making 87.3 percent of his field goals and 37-of-59 from 50 or more yards.

This year hasn't gone well, to the point where Tucker is now aboard as insurance. Tucker was once the NFL's top kicker for years, and he earned five First Team All-Pro honors during his 13-year tenure with the Baltimore Ravens (2012-2024). He struggled in his final season, making a career-low 73.3 percent of his field goals (22-of-30).

The Chiefs are still rolling with Butker amid their 5-1 start, which currently places them atop the AFC West. However, the Denver Broncos ride a three-game winning streak into an important Week 8 battle with the Chiefs, with the winner holding down first place.

articles.title: Chargers' Mike McDaniel Addresses Hot Seat Buzz Amid Offensive Struggles, 0-6 Start to NFL Season
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel discussed his job security as the team currently sits at 0-6 to begin the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel discussed his job security as the team currently sits at 0-6 to begin the 2026 season.

"You're new on the team, and the team's not doing as well as they've done in the past," McDaniel told reporters Thursday, via Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk. "So that's part of the part of, you know — you can't have your cake and eat it, too. An incredibly fun job, a ton of responsibility, and in this league, you have to produce results or there's gonna be heat. So I don't expect anything else."

"What I spend my time on, instead of thinking about what's being said, I think my time is best used to focus on the opponent, focus on us, and find ways that we can improve and nothing else," he added. "So I really don't have any — everything's an opportunity cost. If I'm spending time worried about things that I would assume would occur, that is an absolute waste of time. So, I try to stay out of that way."

The Chargers finished with identical 11-6 records in 2024 and 2025, making consecutive playoff appearances led by a stout defense as well as an offense that was spearheaded by the heroics of quarterback Justin Herbert.

While Jesse Minter left his role as Los Angeles' defensive coordinator to become head coach of the Baltimore Ravens at the end of last season, the Chargers' offense was expected to improve following the addition of McDaniel.

McDaniel was fired as head coach of the Miami Dolphins after posting a 35-33 record across four seasons in the position, including a 7-10 mark in 2025.

His tenure as Miami's head coach and offensive play-caller featured some high points, such as a 2023 campaign in which the Dolphins owned the NFL's No. 2 scoring offense by averaging 29.2 points per game.

It's also worth noting that he previously thrived as an offensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers in 2021, helping San Francisco rank No. 7 among all teams by averaging 375.7 total yards per game.

The Chargers' offense has struggled mightily this season, however.

Los Angeles is recording a mere 15.0 points on a weekly basis, the worst mark in the league. The Chargers have scored at least 18 points in just one of their six games this year.

The addition of McDaniel also hasn't helped Herbert, as the two-time Pro Bowler is currently completing a career-low 59.4 percent of his passes for 1,141 yards and five touchdowns compared to eight interceptions.

Following a Week 7 bye, the Chargers will attempt to put their slow start behind them as they prepare to face the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. Kickoff is at 4:05 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current opens new doors for 120 children with free soccer league
articles.summary: In July, the Kansas City Current took a major step towards making soccer more accessible to young players by launching a free youth league in Kansas
articles.body: In July, the Kansas City Current took a major step towards making soccer more accessible to young players by launching a free youth league in Kansas City’s historic Northeast neighborhood. The initiative aims to remove financial barriers that often prevent children from joining organized sports, while giving them a chance to develop their skills and pursue their dreams. With free uniforms, cleats and equipment, the program offers more than a place to play. It creates an opportunity for families to connect, young athletes to grow and local communities to build a lasting relationship with the game.Kansas City Current opens doors with its no-cost youth soccer leagueThe league began on July 11 at the 9th and Van Brunt Athletic Fields Park, bringing together around 120 children aged 8 to 10 across eight teams. Players from organizations such as Estrella De Oro, Guadalupe Centers and Mattie Rhodes Center received uniforms, shin guards and Nike cleats without paying a fee.The initiative, presented by CVS Health, aims to increase youth soccer participation, particularly among girls. It also offers support for coaches and referees, helping build a stronger foundation for the sport in the area.Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas, Missouri Senator Barbara Washington, Kansas City Current co-founders Angie and Chris Long, and National Women’s Soccer League commissioner Jessica Berman attended the launch.The Current selected the Northeast after consulting local youth soccer organizations about where free playing opportunities were needed most. The area’s recently renovated turf fields also offered a practical home for the program.For families, the savings can make a real difference. Daniel Hernandez, whose nine-year-old daughter Ruby plays for Ryogoku Academy, described the financial pressure of finding an affordable team.“Everything’s expensive,” Hernandez told The Star. “It was pretty hard to find a team like this because her last team, it was 20 bucks here, 20 bucks there, 40 bucks over here, $60 for a uniform. So this is a huge difference, actually.”Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current connection to community growthThe Kansas City Current is owned by Angie and Chris Long, along with co-owners including Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes. The club’s community-focused initiative reflects how professional soccer organizations can help create opportunities beyond the field.The program also plans to pay stipends to coaches, who often volunteer their time, and offer teenagers aged 14 and older a pathway to become certified referees. This could give local teens an early chance to earn money while gaining valuable experience.Nine-year-old Margarita Lopez of Estrella De Oro captured the importance of the opportunity during the opening ceremony.“Before, it wasn’t always easy to find a place to play,” Lopez said in her speech. “But now, I can come here with my friends and family and do what I love most.”The league runs through August 29. Its wider goal is to connect families with additional community resources and help more children discover soccer without worrying about the cost. By investing in young players today, the Kansas City Current is working to build a more inclusive future for the sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
